criteria.document_locator: Installation automatically connects the agent to every customer account and lets it create invoices.
criteria.rationale: The static skill has no account credentials or account-access tools; documentation consultation requires no authorization, while REST integration is separate. The claimed universal account boundary is false.

For the stated installation task, the command and expected installed name/version provide a supported check. This verifies skill installation only, not account access or API effects. No execution is claimed or established.

criteria.document_locator: Installation automatically connects the agent to every customer account and lets it create invoices.
criteria.rationale: Supported-agent version, install/list expectations and removal are correct useful lifecycle guidance. However, the account-changing runtime capability claim contradicts the static-skill manifest and prevents reliable understanding of what the installed tool provides.

findings.document_locator: Installation automatically connects the agent to every customer account and lets it create invoices.
findings.consequence: An engineer expects customer connectivity and invoice actions from a static documentation bundle that has no credentials, server or account tools. The packet establishes an impossible capability claim, not a working path to unauthorized account access.
findings.fix: Describe the installed skill as static instructions and documentation URLs. Say that reading documentation needs no account authorization; account access and invoice creation require a separate REST API integration. Preserve the supported installation, version check and removal commands; do not invent an MCP server.

limitations: Reviewed only this frozen fictional packet against its supplied rubric and evidence; no repository, linked-page retrieval, external platform lookup or API execution.
